help.title: About Stock transfers
help.overview: A stock transfer moves free stock from one warehouse to another. It is a draft until it is completed or cancelled; completing it is the moment the quantities actually move, all lines together.

sections.title: The draft
sections.body: While it is a draft, nothing has left the source warehouse and the document can still change.
items: From and to are both required and must be two different warehouses of this company.
Each line is a product, an optional variant, and a quantity. Every line must be a different, stock-tracked item; a bundle cannot be a line, move its components instead.
Only a draft can be edited, completed, or cancelled.

sections.title: What complete does
sections.body: Complete is all or nothing: one short line refuses the whole transfer and nothing moves.
items: Lines are re-checked first, because products or warehouses may have changed since the draft was saved.
Every line leaves the source and arrives at the destination. Only free stock moves; units reserved for open orders stay where they are.
If the destination has never stocked the item, its inventory row is created.
The ledger gets a transfer-out movement on the source and a transfer-in on the destination, both pointing at this transfer. Done at and done by are recorded.
Completing or cancelling needs permission to write the transfer status.

sections.title: After it is done
sections.body: A completed transfer is history; a cancelled draft never moved anything.
items: Cancel is only from draft, so a completed transfer is not undone here. Create a transfer in the other direction instead.
A completed transfer cannot be deleted. A draft or cancelled one is a soft delete and can be restored.
The Odoo import can bring in internal transfers from Odoo; they arrive already done.
